datasets.name: Water heater installation extras and their usual cost
datasets.description: Permit, expansion tank, venting, gas line, electrical circuit and other add-ons, low / typical / high at U.S. average prices.
datasets.caption: Extras and what they usually cost (U.S. average, before your state factor)
basedOnNames: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778, May 6, 2024)
datasets.tableSource: Hot Water Math installation cost ranges, anchored to the U.S. Department of Energy's 2024 consumer water heater rules (installation costs built from RSMeans) and Home Depot listing prices, and checked against published industry ranges
rows: Permit, haul-away and disposal of the old unit
Typical = DOE's $260 for permitting, removal and disposal; industry guides give $25-$300 for the permit and $100-$500 for removal.
Thermal expansion tank, parts and labor
The tank itself lists for $34-$67 at Home Depot; the rest is about an hour of labor and fittings.
Code items: drain pan, seismic straps, relief valve piping
A drain pan lists for about $12; strapping and drain work are mostly labor. Which items apply depends on your local code.
DOE's earlier estimate was $499 for a non-condensing tankless vent and $263 for a condensing one; industry guides give $300-$1,000.
Gas line upgrade or new gas line
Industry guides give $275-$1,000; a tankless unit often needs a larger line than the tank it replaces.
DOE: "at least several hundred dollars"; industry guides give $300-$800 for electrical work.
DOE's range is about $750-$2,000; typical is the middle of that range.
Moving the heater to a new spot
DOE says relocation can cost up to $2,000; new water, gas or power lines to the new spot are the main cost.
Heat pump space work (louvered door, ducting, condensate pump)
DOE's adders for the most challenging heat pump installs run $0-$4,000 and average $2,000.

rows: DF******* → June 1967, 1987, 2007 or 2027 (latest not in the future)
older tags: 1 letter, then month (2 digits), year (2 digits) and a plant letter
R0804B***** → August 2004 (older tags, often printed as R 0804B…)
older tags: 2 to 4 letters, then month (2 digits) and year (2 digits)
plant letter, then week (2 digits) and year (2 digits)
older all-digit serials: month (2 digits), then year (2 digits)
since 2008: year (2 digits), week (2 digits), then a letter
before 2008: factory letter, month letter, then year (2 digits)
before 2008: month letter, year (2 digits), then a letter
since 2008: year (2 digits), then week (2 digits)
0904******* → 2009, week 4 (Energy Trust labels this example April 2009, which does not match its own year-week rule; we follow the rule)
before 2008: month letter, then year (2 digits)
before mid-2004: factory letter, month letter, then year (2 digits)
9746****** → 1997, week 46 (Energy Trust); 1115…–1631… = April 2011 to August 2016 (CPSC recall range)
4-digit model code and 1 character, then year (2 digits), month (1 character: 1 to 9, X, Y, Z) and day (2 digits)
older tags: 4 digits, a hyphen, then the full date as year (4 digits), month (2) and day (2), a hyphen and 4 more digits
